verdictText: **APPROVE-WITH-NOTES.** The ledger is exact and re-derivable (admission freeze before any edit, product byte-identical to the baseline at the red commit, no test byte changed after the red commit, 13 changed files all registered, 385 of 500 counted lines recomputed, only P2CG1D's own lifecycle fields in units.json). Every carried-forward design rule from the P2CG1C review is met where the unit can meet it: the reservation is write-free, taken inside B's guard after the C IMMEDIATE transaction opened and released in the same synchronous span on both the refusal return and the commit notification; a busy match connection is a typed refusal, never an uncertain commit; duplicates replay before any refusal; the three doors are keyed on the port alone and are byte-for-byte legacy without it; the arbiter keeps a pending approval, its timer and deadline through a refusal and coalesces concurrent approvals into one attempt. All 119 registered cases, the Task 14 selector, the B and C suites, the 35 A1/A2 suites and 164 related suites pass on the exact head; typecheck, lint (87 warnings / 0 errors, identical set), format, lint:units, madge (976 files / 175 chains, identical set), the roadmap validators and OpenSpec all pass. The notes are: one genuine but dormant residual (decision point 1) whose fix lives in B's leaves and must be registered before activation; three coverage pins the author's 16 mutants did not reach (my RM1, RM8, RM9 survived); a C-owned cross-process test that flakes about one run in three on this machine (reproduced); and cosmetic items. Nothing blocks merge.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes, each with the reviewer's section 5 finding verbatim. Authority, privacy, replay and idempotency record no defect. Concurrency records one accepted residual and no active defect: decision point 1 (the admit-then-fail release path relies on P2CG1C's microtask release), carried as CF-E1 and conditioned by the owner ruling on an in-span onNotCommitted hook before P2CG1H activation or an explicit Root acceptance then (H-OPEN-1). Each verdict field is the closure's reading of the finding, not reviewer text.

authority.finding: **Authority.** No defect. The host-only check precedes the host door and the GM-only check precedes the decision door, both unchanged in position. The only activation switch is a server-side typed object installed by code (`installApplicationReceipts`), once, on an empty registry, with no setter and no uninstall; no envelope field, header or boolean reaches it. An approval is tied to the exact pending entry object by identity (`pending.get(proposalId) === entry`), so a timed-out, vetoed or closed proposal cannot be committed by an in-flight approval, and an approval cannot authorise a fresh attempt after an uncertain commit. The late refusal is recognised by exact shape, not by class or name, so a foreign-graph or spoofed object cannot be mistaken for one. The crossGraph case shows a graph that reaches the shared registry cannot substitute its own handle or preparation.

privacy.verdict: PASS (no defect; less exposure than legacy)
privacy.finding: **Privacy.** No defect; strictly less exposure than legacy. Every new wire reason is a kebab-case code from a closed set: the P2CB verdict union (`fresh-request`, `participants-behind`, `correction-pending`, `replacement-artifacts-unverified`, `branch-not-active`, `evidence-unavailable`, `history-integrity`, `context-mismatch`, `gm-required`), B's `append-controls-unsupported`, and D's `proposal-reservation-invalid`, `progression-unsupported`, `progression-reservation-busy`. The `participants-behind` arm's `participantIds` are dropped (RM7 caught); the legacy string sent `participants-behind p1:5,p2:7; requiredRevision 8`. Error frames keep the legacy shape (`code`, `reason`, correlation in the `intentId` field). The shipped client keys on `refusal.code` only (`campaignLifecycleState.ts:494, 588`), so code-only reasons change no client behaviour. The arbiter path's reason is regex-checked on the way out; the host-intent path forwards `outcome.refusal.reason` (typed `string`) unchecked, all of whose sources are constants today (N3).

replay.finding: **Replay.** No defect. No new event type, reducer or journal field; refusals write nothing on C, on `campaign_public_applied_view` or on M (census over the real files is byte-equal before and after each refusal, including the drift refusal that rolls back inside the IMMEDIATE transaction); the committed path is B's unchanged verify-after-apply pipeline; a replayed duplicate answers its committed receipt and appends nothing (two cases).

idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** No defect. Duplicates replay before the guard at two layers (section 4, RM4); `release` and `consume` are idempotent and `afterRelease` re-running after `onCommitted` is a no-op; coalesced approvals produce exactly one guarded attempt (`commit` called once); a late-refused approval leaves the entry pending and a retry starts a fresh attempt without re-arming the timer (RM5 caught); the busy refusal is retryable on the same socket.

concurrency.verdict: PASS WITH ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (no active defect; decision point 1, CF-E1, H-OPEN-1)
concurrency.finding: **Concurrency.** One accepted residual, no active defect. Lock order is C IMMEDIATE (the writer) then M (the reservation inside the guard) on every new door (RM3 caught); M is held across C's COMMIT and released in the commit span (RM2 caught; author's commit-release mutant caught); the span from `reserve()` to either release contains no `await` (the guard, append, COMMIT and `onCommitted` run inside the writer's synchronous `.immediate()`); a throw from `reserve()` is a typed refusal (author's busy mutant caught) and `onCommitted` is always requested, so a borrowed transaction on C is refused by the writer (CF-D7). The host single-writer lock serialises the doors; two concurrent AdvanceDay intents with different ids prepare in parallel and the second's revalidate refuses `fresh-request`; the arbiter's `approving` entry is set before the attempt's first `await`, so a second approve cannot slip between. The residual is decision point 1.

decisionPoint1: **Post-admit append failure relies on C's microtask release.** Confirmed in code: `appendControlledCampaignBatch`'s extend runs the guard, then `append()`; a `revision-conflict` is a result (not a throw), so the transaction function returns, the writer COMMITs an empty transaction and calls the notification wrapper, which returns without calling D's `onCommitted` because `committed === null`; a throw from `append()` rolls C back and propagates to `commit-uncertain`. In both cases M stays in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` past the end of the synchronous span until `holdMatchConnection`'s `queueMicrotask` release runs; `afterRelease` runs later (after `runExclusive` settles) and is a no-op by then. The hazard CF-D1 named is real in principle: any `db.transaction()` write on M that runs in that gap nests as a SAVEPOINT, reports success and is discarded by the ROLLBACK. **Ruling: an accepted residual on this head, not an active defect, with a named owner and a hard condition for activation.** Reasons: (a) the unit is dormant (no production installer; `server.js` untouched), so no production path can hold M at all; (b) the gap is bounded by the microtask queue and opens only on a post-admit append failure, which under the host lock means a second writer process or an I/O error; (c) for a foreign M write to land in the gap it must already be queued as a microtask between the span's enqueue and the C release microtask, which requires a chain started in the same macrotask, and the only same-macrotask companions of a campaign-sync frame are other campaign-sync frames (ws emits same-chunk frames synchronously; finding #78 relies on this), none of which writes M; match sockets, HTTP routes and timers are separate macrotasks. The fix cannot be made in D's leaves: B's extend owns the span. Register, before P2CG1H installs the port, an in-span hook `onNotCommitted?: () => void` on `ICampaignAppendControls` (B leaf `ICampaignEventStore.ts`), invoked synchronously by `appendControlledCampaignBatch` when `appended.kind !== 'committed'` and in a catch around `append()` (B leaf `JournalCampaignEventStore.ts`), passed through `ICampaignCommitControls` unchanged, and wired `onNotCommitted: release` in the binder (D leaf `bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts`, next owners I3 and P2CG2), with a trail case `[BEGIN, guard, ROLLBACK, tick]` for the admit-then-conflict path (RM9 today). P2CG1E's leaves do not include any of these files, so this is either a narrow new registration ahead of H or an explicit Root acceptance recorded at H's admission with this analysis. (CF-E1)

**Duplicate replay before refusal.** Correct and the right precedence: an intent already committed must answer its committed receipt regardless of present readiness, because authority was evaluated when it committed; re-gating a replay would turn an idempotent retry into a spurious refusal. Holds at two layers (doors and store); D's first case pins the observable.

**Port only in an empty registry.** Correct fail-closed design: it makes "an entry built without a launch view beside a flowing receipt port" impossible, which is the invariant the receipt mode needs. Consequence for the activation unit (P2CG1H): `ServerMatchHost.bindCampaignPause` calls `getCampaignHostRegistry().getOrCreate(sessionId)`, so durable active-match recovery in `runtime.bootstrapMultiplayerServer()` (`server.js:537`) can register campaign entries at boot; the install must precede that call, and the campaign SQLite service must be initialised before either, because `register` under an installed port throws when `journalDbOrNull()` is null. Loud failure, correct, but a boot-order trap. (CF-E5)

**C test 1 ms flake.** Reproduced: my run 1 failed `coopMissionCreate.test.ts:1158` (`saga.acquiredAt` 1792271877825 < `times.matchCommit` 1792271877826), runs 2 and 3 passed; the author saw the same 1-in-3. Cause: the parent samples `Date.now()` after `exec('COMMIT')` returns while the child, polling `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` every 2 ms, can acquire and sample within the same millisecond tick, so the two samples can differ by one tick in the wrong direction although the order is real. Not a D concern (the file and the code under test are unchanged by D) but a live CI risk: the case is in the `unit` project that the six CI shards run. Fix in E (owner of the file): sample the parent's `matchCommit` and `campaignRelease` in `traceExec`'s `before` hook instead of `after`, which makes `child.acquiredAt >= parentSample` hold for any monotone shared clock; two lines. (CF-E2)

**Reason-code-only refusals.** Correct; see Privacy. The legacy socket string carried participant ids and acknowledged cursors to the GM; D's carries a code; the client never parsed the string. One hardening left (N3).

**Registry restating the port type.** Acceptable with a note. The restated interface is structurally identical to `campaignApplicationConnection.ts:55-57`; the binder assigns the registry's value into `CampaignApplicationConnection`'s `receipts`, so any drift in the dangerous direction (the original gains a required member or changes `database`'s type) is a compile error at that assignment; drift in the harmless direction (the original relaxes) is undetected and harmless. A type-only import would have added five madge chains because `campaignApplicationConnection` imports the registry. The clean end state is one definition in a neutral module; P2CG1H's planned `campaignApplicationReceiptPort.ts` is that module, and both the registry and the connection should import the type from it then. (CF-E6)
